slides.title: Value = where the market agreed
slides.body: Yesterday NQ built value between 24,430 (VAL) and 24,520 (VAH), POC 24,475. Responsive traders trade back toward value. Initiative traders trade away from it.
slides.tip: Same breakout. Two traders. Only one is right.

slides.title: Responsive sellers at the high
slides.body: Above the VAH sellers hit the bid 3x or more the ask one tick above, three prices in a row. If the bar closes back inside value, the fade is valid.

slides.title: Initiative buyers above value
slides.body: Here buyers lift the ask at 3x or more the bid one tick below, three prices in a row, above 24,520. Delta is strongly positive. Fading this is standing in front of a train.

slides.title: The acceptance test
slides.body: Initiative is confirmed when the pullback holds the VAH, volume builds above it and the POC starts migrating higher. Back inside value with negative delta = it failed.
slides.tip: Hold above = follow. Back inside = fade.

caption:
Above value: fade it or FOLLOW it? 🎯

Every breakout of the value area splits the market in two. Responsive traders sell above value and buy below it, betting on a return to the POC. Initiative traders trade away from value, with aggression, and build new value elsewhere. The footprint shows who is in control. Responsive selling looks like stacked sell imbalances at the high and a close back inside value. Initiative buying looks like the ask lifted at 3x the bid one tick below, three prices in a row, positive delta and a pullback that holds the VAH.

1️⃣ Value area = where the market agreed; trading back toward it is responsive, away from it is initiative
2️⃣ Stacked sell imbalances + close back inside value = the fade is valid
3️⃣ Stacked buy imbalances above the VAH + positive delta = initiative buyers
4️⃣ Confirmation: the pullback holds the VAH and the POC migrates higher
